runs.narrative: I am an explorer stranded on a remote and desolate shingle spit, where the old light-and-weather station once stood. Initially, I navigated the sparse rooms of the station, observing remnants of past activity — a galley with a kettle and a mix of salt and neglect, leading into a store with empty shelves and the scent of paraffin. I traversed back and forth through these dull spaces, my only companions the objects left behind — notably, a coil of rope from the galley which I deemed essential, and an oil can I found in the workshop. With each movement, I was mapping out my surroundings, searching not just for a way out or a means to signal for help, but also seeking any clue that might unravel the history of this forsaken place. My actions, a dance of necessity, guided by the hope that understanding the environment would bring clarity to the situation I found myself in.
